the silylated poly(ethyleneimines) improve simultaneously the coating mechanical performance, the elastic recovery and the resistance to physical ageing.

the silylated hyperbanch poly(ethyleneimines) are a new type of coating with a very high potential to be applied in different fields.
the incorporation of a hyperbranched silylated poly(ethyleneimne) in the epoxy matrix improves simultaneously the coating performance and the recovery.

the use of a hyperbranched polymer as the precursor for the sol–gel reaction leads to coatings with improved mechanical properties.
the use of silylated hyperbranching polymers as a coating modifier can be an interesting alternative to the use of traditional siloxane additives.
